extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty and mathematics educators designing middle-school teacher preparation programs; pre-service middle grades teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for designing college-level mathematics courses, textbooks, and teacher-education programs that prepare prospective middle grades mathematics teachers, including recommended course content, pedagogy, credit requirements, and materials. Focus is on connecting college mathematics to middle school curriculum and on pedagogical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solving course content and emphasis (MTH 499/599)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses should offer students the opportunity to master a variety of problem solving strategies, focus on writing word problems appropriate for middle school students, and on developing and using scoring rubrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly teach strategies such as guess-and-check, tables, diagrams and pictures, exhaustive search, logic, looking for patterns, Venn diagrams, and algebra. Emphasize ratio and percentage problems, rate problems, and work problems because these arise frequently in middle school classrooms. Use coursepacks (example: Cheryl Beaver materials) and provide sample course materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrete mathematics course design for teachers (MTH 497/597)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce discrete mathematics through hands-on activities and connect counting/graph concepts to middle-school-relevant contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early weeks: pigeonhole principle, set theory (including inclusion–exclusion using attribute pieces), arithmetic series. Counting: multiplication rule, permutations, combinations, Pascal’s triangle and binomial theorem—place emphasis on derivation of formulas and relationships. Applications: game-show games, lotteries, poker, 3D Tic-Tac-Toe. Later units: fractals (Sierpinski, Koch) and graph theory (complete/bipartite graphs, trees, vertex coloring, map coloring). Include student presentations of lessons on topics not previously discussed (e.g., Nim, magic squares). For graduate-level versions, increase emphasis on proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content pedagogy course focus (ED 434/ED 436)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses on content pedagogy should focus on the process of teaching mathematics and the NCTM Principles: Equity, Curriculum, Teaching, Learning, Assessment, and Technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with comparisons between national standards (NCTM) and state standards (Common Core). Use classroom activities like discussions, exploration of mathematical tasks, student presentations, and readings. Assignments should include designing problem-based lessons, analyzing video of practicing teachers, creating proficiency-based assessments, reflecting on mathematics education research, analyzing individual teaching practice, and modifying curriculum to raise cognitive demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations sequence goals and pedagogy (MTH 211–213)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations courses should give students a deeper understanding of basic topics (whole numbers, integers, fractions, geometry, probability/statistics) focusing on why rules are true and on correcting misconceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use group work/discovery-based learning style, extensive use of manipulatives, and tasks that require conceptual clarification rather than rote procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary problem solving practices (MTH 396)
rubrics_metrics.description: A course focused on problem solving should have students practice a variety of techniques, create word problems appropriate to a given strategy, and assess student problem solving via mentoring/field work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include opportunities to craft and diagnose word problems, and to assess others' problem solving through mentoring programs with local elementary school children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with state licensure and testing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs must align coursework and authorization-level requirements with state licensure tests and endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required education department courses (e.g., ED 434/436), ensure students take required state tests (e.g., CBEST, ORELA, National Evaluation Series Middle School Mathematics test where applicable), and specify which mathematics courses are required for each authorization level (elementary, middle, middle/high with math focus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended amount of mathematical coursework (MET report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective teachers should take a minimum recommended amount of mathematics coursework depending on the licensure level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: elementary grade teachers — at least 9 semester-hours on fundamental ideas of elementary school mathematics; middle grade teachers — at least 21 semester-hours of mathematics including at least 12 semester-hours on fundamental ideas of school mathematics appropriate for middle grade teachers; high school teachers — equivalent of an undergraduate major in mathematics including a 6-hour capstone connecting college and high school mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course focus: deep understanding and habits of mind (MET)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses should focus on thorough development of basic mathematical ideas and on developing habits of mind necessary for mathematical thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond content, courses should develop flexible, interactive teaching styles, promote thinking like a mathematical thinker, and emphasize the quality of mathematical preparation over sheer quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental mission and faculty involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher education should be recognized as an important part of mathematics departments' mission, with mathematicians actively involved in K–12 mathematics education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage more mathematicians to participate deeply in teacher preparation, and structure programs so mathematics faculty and mathematics-education faculty teach complementary components (math content by math faculty; methods/field experience by math-education faculty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core curriculum connecting college and middle school mathematics (.CM/2 Project)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a core of undergraduate mathematics courses that explicitly connect college-level mathematics with middle school curriculum topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example core: algebra & number theory, geometric structures, data analysis & probability, mathematics of change (calculus connections). These 12 credits form the core of a larger content requirement; other standard math courses supplement the core. Offer cross-listed/extended versions for in-service teachers seeking graduate credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of middle-grade curricular materials as a design feature of textbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Textbooks for prospective teachers should use current middle grade mathematics curricular materials in multiple ways to connect college mathematics to school mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses include: as a springboard to college-level mathematics; to expose future teachers to middle-grade curricula; to motivate deeper mathematics; to support curriculum dissection and lesson study; to use college content to gain new perspectives on middle grade content; and to apply middle grade instructional strategies and multiple forms of assessment in college classrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook components: Classroom Connections, Discussions, and Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher-focused textbooks should include Classroom Connections (middle grade investigations), Classroom Discussions (mathematical conversations to introduce concepts), and Classroom Problems (problems with complete/partial solutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design these components so they serve as launch pads to college-level material, engage pre-service teachers in problem solving, and help connect what is learned in college to what will be taught in the middle grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional method: small-group investigations and formalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use small working groups to investigate middle-grade lessons, followed by whole-class reporting and formalization of mathematical ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have groups investigate a middle-grade curriculum unit, report methods and findings to the class, then reflect and formalize definitions and terminology. Integrate extension work (e.g., expressing LCM/GCD via prime factors, Euclid's algorithm, writing GCD as a linear combination) across multiple class periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of student lesson presentations and technology in geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Require pre-service teachers to prepare and deliver lessons from middle-grade geometry curricula, and incorporate dynamic geometry software as a teaching aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team presentations help ensure teachers thoroughly understand middle-grade materials and their connection to college-level content. Introduce tools like Geometer’s Sketchpad to study similarity, transformations, and to model classroom uses of technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment practice: develop and use scoring rubrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses should include instruction and practice in developing and using scoring rubrics for assessing student work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly teach rubric development tied to problem-solving tasks and use those rubrics to evaluate student-created word problems and problem-solving performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on derivation and proofs where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant (e.g., discrete mathematics, advanced/graduate offerings), place emphasis on derivation of formulas and proof-based understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive formulas for permutations and combinations and relate them to the binomial theorem; in graduate courses emphasize formal proofs and theoretical understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure, credit, and performance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify program credit-hour structure, required course lists, capstone experiences, and minimum GPA thresholds for endorsements/licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a 29-credit content requirement (University of Missouri example), a 24-credit middle-school minor at UWO consisting of required 3-course sequence plus electives and a capstone seminar, and a required 3.0 GPA in program courses to obtain licensure endorsement. Include field experiences (e.g., TDP 4364/TDP 4374) as part of methods courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program effectiveness evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate courses and materials by their effect on teachers' mathematical content knowledge, teaching practice, and ability to use collaborative and student-centered approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and analyze participant feedback and evaluator data to assess whether courses helped teachers expand/deepen content knowledge, facilitate learning, improve teaching practice via collaborative learning strategies and lesson study, and provide usable classroom resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program philosophy: constructivist stance and mathematizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a constructivist philosophy that treats learning as participation in a culture of mathematizing rather than mere transmission of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design courses to help future teachers view mathematics as a human activity of making sense of patterns, to develop capacity to make judgments about students' conjectures, construct counterexamples, and create examples/non-examples; support participation in the practices of a mathematics classroom.
